brief.topic: Write a tool description your agent can't misread
brief.audience: PMs and engineers building tool-using agents
constraints: Tool spec is a fictional example; error counts are illustrative and labelled on screen and in caption

coreInsight: Agents choose tools from the descriptions you write, so spell out what each tool does, when to use it, when not to and what to use instead, its required arguments, limits and what it returns.

caption.opening: Agents pick tools and fill in arguments from the descriptions you write. A one-line description leaves the model guessing.
body:
For every tool, write:
→ What it does (and its scope: one order, not many)
→ When to use it
→ When NOT to, and which tool to use instead
→ Required arguments and where they come from
→ Limits, like a maximum amount
→ What it returns, including errors
Then test it: run your agent test cases and count wrong tool calls before and after.
Still enforce limits in code. A description guides the model; it doesn’t stop it.
(The tool spec is a made-up example; 9 vs 2 wrong calls is illustrative.)

claims.text: Detailed tool descriptions that state purpose, when to use and not use the tool, argument requirements, limits and return values reduce wrong tool selection and bad arguments in agents.
9 wrong calls out of 50 test requests with a one-line description vs 2 with a full description.
